title: Consistent Modified Gravity Weak Lensing in Energy-Flow Cosmology: The µ–Σ Eigenmode, Destructive Interference, and E_G as the Orthogonal Probe
description: Derives the observable eigenstructure of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) for weak lensing in a consistent modified-gravity setup (Case B) where µ(k,z) affects growth and Σ(k,z) affects the lensing kernel. Shows analytically that weak lensing constrains only a single effective parameter η_eff = γ(µ−1) + (Σ−1), with growth suppression cancelling 66% of the lensing boost. Proves that E_G measures Σ/µ^γ and is orthogonal to weak lensing, predicting E_G^EFC/E_G^GR = 1.086.

key_results.main_finding: Weak lensing constrains only η_eff = γ(µ−1) + (Σ−1), leading to destructive interference where µ<1 cancels 66% of the Σ>1 lensing boost; EG is the orthogonal probe predicting E_G^EFC/E_G^GR = 1.086.

kill_criteria: KC1: Weak-lensing-only Case B analysis (KiDS-1000 scales, ℓ ≲ 100) yields η_eff inconsistent with 0.017 by >3σ at the EFC anchor.
KC2: The WL-only posterior correlation corr(µ0, Σ0) falls outside [−0.95, −0.80], indicating the predicted µ–Σ eigenmode is not realized.
KC3: A robust EG measurement finds E_G^EFC/E_G^GR inconsistent with 1.086 by >3σ at k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc and z ≲ 0.5.
KC4: Case B WL-only fit prefers EFC over GR (or vice versa) with |Δχ²| > 6, contradicting the predicted near-null WL signal (−2 ≤ Δχ² ≤ +2).
KC5: The observed WL scale/redshift dependence contradicts the EFC localization (signal concentrated at ℓ ≲ 100 and ξ+(θ > 1°), with negligible effect in ξ− and at ℓ ≳ 200).

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This T2 sealed-prediction paper formalizes the consistent (Case B) weak-lensing response of EFC in modified gravity, proving that cosmic shear constrains only the µ–Σ eigenmode η_eff = γ(µ−1) + (Σ−1), with a 66% destructive cancellation of the naïve lensing boost. It identifies E_G as the orthogonal probe (measuring Σ/µ^γ) and registers five sealed numerical predictions, including a near-null WL-only Δχ² and a precise E_G ratio of 1.086. This reframes WL expectations for EFC, redirects emphasis to low-ℓ shear and E_G, and sets concrete falsifiers without closing existing theory or priority gaps.
graph_insights: Introduces the explicit µ–Σ eigenmode in EFC with destructive interference, aligning with concepts: weak lensing, mu–Sigma degeneracy, eigenmode, destructive interference.
Positions E_G as the orthogonal observable linking cosmic shear, growth index γ, and RSD, creating a bridge to growth-based validations.
No prior related papers at 1–2 hops: this is the first consistent WL Case B derivation in the EFC corpus, defining new test vectors in the graph.

implicit_consequences: Any large WL-only fit improvement from a phenomenological Σ-rescaling (Case A) is expected to disappear under consistent Case B due to µ–Σ cancellation.
WL alone cannot separate µ and Σ; E_G becomes decisive for breaking the degeneracy and testing EFC at low z and k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc.
Analysis priority shifts to low-ℓ shear and ξ+ scales for sensitivity; ξ− and high-ℓ contribute negligible EFC signal and should be de-emphasized for detection power.
Strong WL-only preference for either EFC or GR would contradict the Case B prediction and trigger a kill condition.
RSD-quality pipelines gain higher priority since E_G requires robust fσ8 inputs; this reinforces urgency for RSD/EG cross-pipeline readiness.
